draft.title: The double helix
card: DNA is made of two long strands twisted around each other. This shape is called a double helix, like a twisted ladder.
Each strand is a chain of units that carry a base. The four bases are A, T, C and G. The bases of the two strands face each other in the middle.
Bases pair in a fixed way: A with T, and C with G. So if one strand reads A, A, C, the other strand reads T, T, G.

The structure was worked out using the work of Rosalind Franklin, Maurice Wilkins, James Watson and Francis Crick. Franklin and Wilkins made X-ray images of DNA, and Watson and Crick built the model of the double helix.
draft.remember: DNA is a twisted ladder of two strands, with A pairing with T and C with G.

a.q: One strand of DNA has the base sequence G, A, T, C. What is the matching sequence on the other strand?
a.why: Each base pairs with a fixed partner: G with C, A with T, T with A and C with G. This gives C, T, A, G. Copying the same sequence is tempting, but a base never pairs with itself.
a.clue: Pair each base with its partner, one at a time.

b.q: A scientist tests a sample of DNA and finds that 30% of its bases are A. What percentage of its bases are C?
b.why: A pairs with T, so 30% of the bases are T as well. That makes 60% A and T, leaving 40% for C and G together. C and G pair, so each is 20%. Choosing 40% forgets that C and G share that amount.
b.clue: Find T first, then share what is left between C and G.

wants.brief: A double helix of DNA drawn as a twisted ladder. Two twisting strands are joined by rungs in the middle. Label the two strands and the bases. Show the pairs A with T and C with G.
wants.why: Seeing the twisted ladder and the paired bases makes the structure easier to understand.

problems.detail: G, A, T, C is its own reverse complement. Read in its own direction (antiparallel), the partner strand is also G, A, T, C, so the distractor 'G, A, T, C' is defensible for a student who knows more. A non-palindromic sequence would remove this.

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate, and the intended answers (C, T, A, G and 20%) are correct. The one minor issue: question a's sequence G, A, T, C is palindromic, so the 'copy the same sequence' distractor is technically the partner strand read antiparallel. A different sequence would avoid this.
